create.title: Best Chatbot for Customer Service in 2026: 9 Tools Compared
create.excerpt: Nine customer service chatbots compared by how they work, who answers, where your data lives and how you pay.
create.content:
The best chatbot for customer service is the one that matches how your business answers questions today. A support team with agents online needs something different from a shop owner who answers email at night. This guide compares nine tools by how they are built, not by feature lists that change every month.

On this page

  1. How we compared these tools
  2. Quick picks
  3. The 9 tools, one by one
  4. The real decision: who answers?
  5. Where your customer data lives
  6. How the pricing models compare
  7. How to choose in an afternoon
  8. Frequently asked questions

How we compared these tools

Prices and plans change often, so we leave them out and describe each tool in general terms from public information, last reviewed in October 2026. Check each vendor's own site before you decide. We looked at four questions that decide most choices:

  • Who answers? People on your team, an AI, or both.
  • Where does the answer come from? A knowledge base you write, flows you design, or the pages you already publish.
  • Where do chats and leads live? On the vendor's servers or in your own website.
  • How do you pay? Per agent seat, per conversation or resolution, per contact, or a yearly license.

We build Talkwyn, one of the nine, so read our take with that in mind. We say where another tool is the better fit.

Quick picks

If you needLook at
AI answers from your WordPress pages, data on your siteTalkwyn
Live chat, email and social messages in one hosted inboxTidio, Crisp
A full support platform with tickets and in-app messagesIntercom, Zendesk
Messaging on WhatsApp and other apps with agentsFreshchat
Chat that feeds a CRMHubSpot
Human live chat for a team that is online all dayLiveChat, tawk.to

The 9 tools, one by one

1. Talkwyn. An AI chatbot that runs inside WordPress. It scans your published pages, posts, WooCommerce products and Elementor content, answers in the visitor's language with source links, and offers lead capture when a visitor shows interest. Chats and leads stay in your WordPress database. You bring a free or paid AI key. Best for small businesses and shops on WordPress. Not for teams that need human live chat or tickets.

2. Tidio. A hosted tool that combines live chat, a multichannel inbox, visual automation flows and an AI agent billed by conversations. Best for small online shops that want people and AI in one inbox. See our Tidio comparison.

3. Intercom. A customer service platform with an inbox, tickets, a help center, in-app messages and an AI agent priced per resolution on top of seats. Best for software companies with support teams. See the Intercom comparison.

4. Zendesk. A help desk built around tickets from email, phone and chat, with macros, service levels and AI features for larger teams. Best for support departments. See the Zendesk comparison.

5. Freshchat. Messaging for support teams across your website and apps such as WhatsApp, inside the Freshworks suite, with AI sessions billed on top of agent seats. Best for teams answering on several channels. See the Freshchat comparison.

6. Crisp. A shared inbox for chat, email and social messages, priced per workspace, with AI features that come with a credit allowance. Best for small teams that reply every day. See the Crisp comparison.

7. LiveChat. Live chat software for agents, priced per seat, with routing, canned responses and reports. AI answers usually come from a separate product. Best for sales and support teams online all day. See the LiveChat comparison.

8. tawk.to. Free human live chat, with paid add-ons such as an AI assistant and branding removal. Best when someone is ready to reply during the day and budget is tight. See the tawk.to comparison.

9. HubSpot. Chat and a chatbot builder inside the HubSpot CRM, where conversations become contacts and deals. Best for businesses that already run on HubSpot. See the HubSpot comparison.

The real decision: who answers?

Most customer service chatbots fall into two groups. In the first, the chat is a door to your team: an agent, or an AI that hands over to an agent. These tools shine when people are online, and they charge for seats or resolutions because people and AI time cost money.

In the second group, the chatbot does the answering itself, from content you control. That suits businesses where nobody is free to sit in an inbox, and where most questions are already answered somewhere on the website: prices, opening hours, delivery, returns, services.

A quick test: read your last twenty customer emails. If most could be answered by a page you already have, start with an AI chatbot that reads your site. If most need a person to look something up, start with live chat or a help desk.

Where your customer data lives

Hosted tools keep conversations on the vendor's servers. That is convenient, and it means your customer history lives in an account you rent. A chatbot installed in your own site, like Talkwyn on WordPress, keeps chats and leads in your database. Messages still go to the AI provider you choose to generate answers, so read that provider's terms too. Our chatbot privacy checklist lists what to ask any vendor.

How the pricing models compare

Instead of comparing list prices, compare the shape of the bill. Per-seat pricing grows with your team. Per-conversation or per-resolution pricing grows with your traffic. Contact-based pricing grows with your list. A yearly license stays flat. Work out what each model costs over three years at your expected volume. The Talkwyn pricing page shows that math for our plans.

How to choose in an afternoon

  1. Write down the ten questions customers ask most, in the languages they use.
  2. Shortlist two tools from the quick picks that match who answers in your business.
  3. Install or sign up for both, and ask each the same ten questions.
  4. Compare the answers, whether they cite a source, and what happens when the answer is unknown.
  5. Check where the leads go and who will follow up.

If WordPress is your platform, you can add a free AI chatbot to WordPress in about five minutes and test it next to your current tool.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best chatbot for customer service for a small business?

If you have no support team and your answers are on your website, an AI chatbot that reads your site is usually the best start. If people answer chats all day, a live chat tool fits better.

Can a chatbot replace my support team?

No. A good chatbot answers repeat questions and collects leads, so your team spends time on the conversations that need a person.

Which customer service chatbot works with WordPress?

Most hosted tools add a widget to WordPress. Talkwyn is a WordPress plugin that reads your pages and products directly and keeps data in your database.

Do I need to write a knowledge base first?

Not with Talkwyn: it answers from the pages you already publish. Help desk tools usually ask you to write help articles.

create.title: Is the Gemini API Key Free? Limits and How to Get One
create.excerpt: How to get a Gemini API key, what the free tier means for a website chatbot, and when to add a second provider.
create.content:
Yes, you can get a Gemini API key for free. Google offers a free tier for the Gemini API through Google AI Studio, with rate limits that Google sets for each model. This guide shows how to get the key, what the free tier means in practice, and how to use it to power a website chatbot.

On this page

  1. Is the Gemini API key free?
  2. How to get a Gemini API key
  3. What the free limits mean for a chatbot
  4. How to use your Gemini key in Talkwyn
  5. When to move beyond the free tier
  6. Frequently asked questions

Is the Gemini API key free?

Creating a key costs nothing, and the free tier lets you call Gemini models without a credit card. The catch is limits: Google caps how many requests you can send per minute and per day, and the numbers differ by model. Google changes them from time to time, so check the current rate limits page in the Gemini API documentation instead of trusting a number in a blog post, including this one.

Google also has a paid tier, billed through a Google Cloud account, with higher limits. Read Google's terms for each tier, too: the terms for free, unpaid use differ from the paid terms in how Google may use the content you send. If your chatbot will handle customer messages, decide which tier fits before launch.

How to get a Gemini API key

  1. Sign in to Google AI Studio with a Google account.
  2. Open the API keys section and create a new key. You may be asked to pick or create a Google Cloud project.
  3. Copy the key and keep it private, like a password.
  4. Paste it only into the settings of the tool that will use it, never into a page or a public file.
Treat an API key like a password. Anyone who has it can spend your quota or, on a paid plan, your money. If a key leaks, delete it in Google AI Studio and create a new one.

What the free limits mean for a chatbot

Each visitor message to an AI chatbot is at least one request. A small business site with a few dozen chats a day often stays within a free tier. A busy shop on a sale day may not. When a provider hits its limit, a chatbot that depends on one key simply stops answering.

That is why we recommend two providers. In Talkwyn you can add Gemini next to Groq, OpenRouter or Cloudflare Workers AI, put them in the order you like, and Talkwyn moves to the next one automatically when one fails or hits its limit. The free AI API keys guide compares all four.

How to use your Gemini key in Talkwyn

  1. Install Talkwyn on your WordPress site. The setup wizard opens.
  2. Pick Google Gemini, paste your key and click Test. You can load the list of models from Google or type a model name.
  3. Click Scan my site so Talkwyn reads your pages, posts and products.
  4. Choose your colour and welcome message, and turn the chat on.

One difference to know: with Talkwyn Pro, most providers stream replies word by word, while Gemini and Cloudflare reply in one go. The answer is the same; it just appears at once. Settings for every provider are in the AI provider settings guide.

When to move beyond the free tier

  • Visitors see the fallback reply often because every provider is at its limit.
  • You need the terms of a paid tier for customer data.
  • You want a specific paid model. Talkwyn Pro adds OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Mistral and DeepSeek.

Until then, two free providers with automatic fallback are enough for many small sites.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Gemini API completely free?

There is a free tier with rate limits set by Google, and a paid tier with higher limits. Check Google's current limits and terms.

Do I need a credit card for a Gemini API key?

At the time of writing, Google AI Studio does not ask for one for the free tier. The paid tier is billed through a Google Cloud account.

Can I use a Gemini API key for a website chatbot?

Yes. Talkwyn supports Gemini in the free plugin. Add a second provider so the chat keeps answering when one hits its limit.

Where is my key stored in Talkwyn?

In your WordPress settings. Talkwyn never prints keys in your pages.

create.title: Self-Hosted Chatbot for Your Website: Keep Chats and Leads at Home
create.excerpt: What "self-hosted" means for a website chatbot, what stays on your server, and what still leaves it.
create.content:
A self-hosted chatbot runs on your own website instead of on a vendor's servers. For most small businesses that means one thing in practice: chats and leads are stored in your own database, under your own backups and your own privacy policy. This guide explains what self-hosting covers, what it does not, and how to set it up on WordPress.

On this page

  1. What "self-hosted" means for a chatbot
  2. What stays on your server with Talkwyn
  3. What still leaves your server
  4. Why businesses choose a self-hosted chatbot
  5. How to set up a self-hosted chatbot on WordPress
  6. Frequently asked questions

What "self-hosted" means for a chatbot

A chatbot has three parts: the chat window your visitors see, the place where conversations and leads are stored, and the AI model that writes the answers. A hosted chatbot runs the first two on the vendor's servers and usually picks the AI for you. A self-hosted chatbot runs the window and the storage on your site.

The AI model is the part to be honest about. Running a large language model on your own server needs hardware that most websites do not have. So most self-hosted website chatbots, Talkwyn included, still send each question to an AI provider you choose, along with the matching text from your site, to write the answer.

What stays on your server with Talkwyn

  • Chats, if you keep logs on. They are deleted after 30 days by default, or never stored if you turn logs off.
  • Leads, with the visitor's question and the page they came from, until you delete them. You can export them as CSV.
  • The index of your pages, posts and products that answers are built from.
  • Your settings and AI keys.

Talkwyn also works with the WordPress personal data export and erase tools, so you can answer a visitor who asks for their data.

What still leaves your server

  • The visitor's message, recent conversation and matching page text go to the AI provider you picked, to generate the answer.
  • Lead emails go through your site's email setup to your inbox.
  • With Pro, if you set them up, new leads are posted to Slack or Telegram.
  • If you add Cloudflare Turnstile keys, the lead form's spam check talks to Cloudflare.

Nothing goes to talkwyn.com from your visitors' chats. The free plugin only contacts talkwyn.com if you tick the news opt-in in the setup wizard, which is unticked by default.

Why businesses choose a self-hosted chatbot

  • Ownership. Customer conversations are business records. They stay in the database you already back up.
  • One privacy story. You describe one system in your privacy policy, plus the AI provider you chose.
  • No account to lose. If you stop paying for Pro, the free plugin keeps working with all your data.
  • Your choice of AI. Pick the provider whose terms suit you, and change it any time.

How to set up a self-hosted chatbot on WordPress

  1. Install Talkwyn and open the setup wizard.
  2. Paste an AI key. Pick a provider whose data terms you are comfortable with.
  3. Click Scan my site. Only public, published content is read; drafts, users and passwords never are.
  4. Set the log retention under Talkwyn, Privacy, and turn on the privacy notice in the chat.
  5. Mention the chatbot and your AI provider in your own privacy policy.

Our chatbot privacy checklist goes through the questions to ask about any chatbot, hosted or not.

Frequently asked questions

Is Talkwyn fully self-hosted?

The chat, storage and index run in your WordPress site. Answers are written by the AI provider you choose, so messages go to that provider.

Can I run the AI model on my own server?

Not with Talkwyn today. It connects to cloud AI providers such as Groq, Google Gemini, OpenRouter and Cloudflare Workers AI, and with Pro OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Mistral and DeepSeek.

How long are chats kept?

30 days by default. You can change the number of days or turn logs off. Leads stay until you delete them.

What happens to my data if I uninstall?

It stays unless you turn on "Delete all Talkwyn data" before uninstalling.

The best chatbot for ecommerce answers the questions that stop people from buying: is it in stock, what does shipping cost, can I return it, where is my order. This guide lists what to look for, how to test it on your own store, and where Talkwyn fits for WooCommerce shops.

On this page

  1. 1. It answers from your real product data
  2. 2. It knows your shipping and returns pages
  3. 3. It can look up an order safely
  4. 4. It shows products, not only text
  5. 5. It never invents a price or a policy
  6. 6. It speaks your shoppers' languages
  7. 7. It does not slow the store down
  8. 8. Its pricing does not punish a busy season
  9. How to test an ecommerce chatbot
  10. Frequently asked questions

1. It answers from your real product data

A shopper asking "does the large backpack come in green?" needs your actual attributes, not a guess. Look for a chatbot that reads product titles, descriptions, prices, stock status and attributes directly from your store, and keeps up when you change them. Talkwyn reads WooCommerce products this way and updates its index when you save a product.

2. It knows your shipping and returns pages

Shipping and returns questions are the most common pre-sale questions in most stores. A chatbot can only answer them well if the pages are clear. Our guide to shipping and returns pages a chatbot can answer shows how to write them.

3. It can look up an order safely

"Where is my order?" is the top question after a sale. Talkwyn Pro answers it when the shopper gives the order number and the billing email, and shows status, date, total, items and tracking numbers. It allows five tries per hour, so nobody can guess their way through your orders.

4. It shows products, not only text

When the answer is a product, showing it helps. Talkwyn Pro adds up to three product cards under an answer, with image, price, stock, a View product button, and Add to cart for simple products in stock.

5. It never invents a price or a policy

A chatbot that makes up a discount creates a customer service problem. Look for one that answers business questions only from your content, shows the source, and says so when the answer is not there.

6. It speaks your shoppers' languages

Cross-border shoppers write in their own language. Talkwyn replies in the language of each message, from your existing pages, and works with WPML and Polylang if your store is translated. See the multilingual chatbot page for the details.

7. It does not slow the store down

Checkout speed is money. The chat script should load after the page and stay out of checkout. Talkwyn's script loads after the page, talks to your server only when someone sends a message, and can be hidden on checkout and thank-you pages.

8. Its pricing does not punish a busy season

Per-conversation pricing grows with your best days. A flat yearly license does not. With Talkwyn the plugin is free, Pro is one yearly license, and AI usage goes to the provider you choose.

How to test an ecommerce chatbot

  1. List twenty real questions from your inbox and reviews: stock, sizes, shipping, returns, payment, order status.
  2. Ask each one, and a few in another language.
  3. Check that every answer matches your store and links to the right page.
  4. Ask about something you do not sell. The chatbot should say so.

create.content:
These real estate chatbot examples show how a website chatbot handles the questions buyers, sellers and renters ask an agency, and how a good conversation ends with a lead in your inbox. The conversations are samples we wrote to show the pattern, based on how Talkwyn behaves; they are not quotes from real customers.

On this page

  1. How these conversations work
  2. Seven examples
  3. What the good conversations have in common
  4. Set this up on your agency site
  5. Frequently asked questions

How these conversations work

Talkwyn answers from your listings and pages, in the visitor's language. When a visitor asks for a viewing, a valuation or a call, or after a few real questions, it asks whether they would like the team to follow up and shows a short form inside the chat. The lead arrives by email with the visitor's question and the page they were on.

Seven examples

1. The viewing request. A buyer on a listing asks: "Can I see this on Saturday morning?" The chatbot answers what the listing says about viewings, then offers: "Would you like the team to contact you to arrange a time?" The buyer leaves a name, email and phone. The agent replies within the hour.

2. The parking question. "Does the flat come with parking?" The listing mentions one allocated space, so the chatbot answers and links the listing. The buyer asks two more questions about service charges and the lease, then accepts a follow-up.

3. The valuation. A homeowner asks: "How much is my house worth?" The chatbot does not guess a price. It explains what your valuation page says about the process and offers to have an agent get in touch. Seller leads like this are often the most valuable.

4. The renter at midnight. "Are pets allowed?" asked at 11:40 at night. The rental listing says pets are considered on request, so that is the answer. The renter asks to be contacted in the morning, and the lead is waiting when the office opens.

5. The overseas buyer. A buyer writes in Spanish about a holiday apartment. The chatbot answers in Spanish from your English listing, with the source, and collects their details in Spanish too.

6. The area question. "Is this close to a good school?" If your area guide covers schools, the chatbot answers from it. If not, it says it does not have that information and offers a follow-up. That gap is a hint to write an area page.

7. The mortgage question. "Can you help with a mortgage?" If you list partner brokers on a services page, the chatbot answers from that page and offers an introduction. It never gives financial advice.

What the good conversations have in common

  • They start with a real answer, not a form.
  • The offer to follow up comes when the visitor shows intent.
  • The lead carries the visitor's question, so the agent knows what to say first.
  • Missing answers become content: every "I do not have that" points to a page worth writing.

Set this up on your agency site

  1. Make sure each listing has the facts buyers ask about: parking, pets, service charges, viewing times.
  2. Write an area guide and a valuation page.
  3. Install Talkwyn, paste a free AI key, and click Scan my site.
  4. Ask the seven questions above and fix the gaps.

The real estate chatbot template has a checklist for listings and pages, and the real estate chatbot page shows the full setup.

Frequently asked questions

Are these real customer conversations?

No. They are samples we wrote to show how Talkwyn behaves. Your results depend on your pages and your visitors.

Can the chatbot book viewings in my calendar?

No. Talkwyn does not connect to calendars. It collects the visitor's details so your team can arrange the viewing.

Will it give a price for a valuation?

No. It answers only from your pages and never invents a price.

How fast do I get the lead?

The lead email is sent the moment the visitor submits the form. With Pro it can also go to Slack or Telegram.

create.title: Healthcare Chatbot Use Cases for Clinics
create.excerpt: Where a website chatbot helps a clinic, where it must stop, and how to set it up with privacy in mind.
create.content:
Healthcare chatbot use cases are less about diagnosis and more about the front desk. Most calls and emails a clinic receives are practical: opening hours, services, insurance, parking, what to bring. This guide lists the use cases that work on a clinic website, the ones a chatbot should never take on, and how to set one up carefully.

On this page

  1. Use cases that work
  2. What a clinic chatbot should never do
  3. Privacy first
  4. How to know it is working
  5. Setup in an afternoon
  6. Frequently asked questions

Use cases that work

  • Opening hours and holidays. "Are you open on Saturday?" answered from your hours page.
  • Services. "Do you do children's check-ups?" answered from your services pages, with a link.
  • Insurance and payment. Which plans you accept, if your site lists them.
  • New patients. How to register, what to bring, which forms to fill in.
  • Getting there. Address, parking, public transport, accessibility.
  • Appointment requests. The visitor leaves their details and your team calls back.
  • Other languages. Patients who write in another language get an answer in that language, from your pages.

What a clinic chatbot should never do

  • Give medical or dental advice, or interpret symptoms.
  • Handle emergencies. Your site should say clearly what to do in an emergency.
  • Collect detailed health information in a chat form.
  • Promise appointment times it cannot see.

Talkwyn answers business questions only from your published pages and does not connect to booking calendars or patient records. Write your emergency and medical-advice notice on a page, and add it to your welcome message.

Privacy first

Talkwyn makes no compliance claims for health data regulations such as HIPAA, so set it up so that health details are not asked for:

  • Keep the lead form to name, email and phone, and use the consent checkbox.
  • Shorten chat log retention, or turn logs off, under Talkwyn, Privacy.
  • Show the privacy notice in the chat.
  • Hide the chat on pages where it does not belong.
  • Mention the chatbot and your AI provider in your privacy policy.

The chatbot privacy checklist covers the questions to ask before launch.

How to know it is working

Count the calls and emails about hours, parking and insurance before and after launch. With Pro, the analytics and unanswered questions inbox show what patients ask and which answers are missing from your site, so you can add them.

Setup in an afternoon

  1. Check that hours, services, insurance, new patient steps and directions are on published pages.
  2. Install Talkwyn, paste a free AI key and click Scan my site.
  3. Write a welcome message that says what the chat can help with, and what it cannot.
  4. Ask twenty real front-desk questions and fix the gaps.

For a worked example, read the chatbot for dental clinics guide or the healthcare chatbot page.

Frequently asked questions

Can a chatbot give medical advice?

It should not. Talkwyn answers practical questions from your published pages and is not built for medical advice.

Is Talkwyn HIPAA compliant?

We make no HIPAA claim. Set up the chat so that health details are not collected, and check your obligations with an adviser.

Can patients book appointments in the chat?

They can leave their details for a callback. Talkwyn does not connect to booking calendars.

Does it answer in other languages?

Yes. It replies in the language the patient writes in, from your pages.

What white label means with Talkwyn

On the Agency plan, the WordPress admin shows your logo and your menu name instead of Talkwyn, and the chat menu can link to your agency. The "Powered by Talkwyn" badge in the chat is off by default on every plan, so visitors see only your client's brand. You can also export the settings from one site and import them on the next.

One Agency license covers unlimited client sites, and staging sites never count. Each client's chats and leads stay in that client's own WordPress database. More on the white label chatbot for agencies page.

  • Setup. Install, scan, style it to the brand, write the welcome message, test twenty questions. A one-off fee.
  • Care. Monthly check of unanswered questions, new pages for the gaps, and a short report. A monthly fee on the care plan.
  • Languages. A multilingual chatbot for clients with international customers, from the same pages.
  • Leads. Lead email to the client, and with Pro Slack or Telegram alerts.

How to price it

Your cost is one Agency license per year, [tw_value key="price_agency"], plus AI usage, which each client can pay with their own key or stay within a free tier. As an example, if you add $20 a month for the chatbot to each care plan, a handful of clients covers the yearly license and the rest is margin for your time. Set your price by the time you spend on setup and care, not by the license.

Tip: let each client create their own AI key in their name. The usage, limits and terms then sit with the client, and you avoid paying for their traffic.

Roll it out client by client

  1. Set up one site completely and export the settings.
  2. On the next client site, install Talkwyn and Pro, activate your Agency key, and import the settings.
  3. Add the client's AI key, click Scan my site, and adjust colours and the welcome message.
  4. Test on staging first; staging never counts toward your sites.

Most chatbot support is content: a wrong or missing answer means a page is missing or unclear. With Pro, the unanswered questions inbox lists those gaps, with Add answer and Dismiss buttons. A monthly look at it is the core of a chatbot care service. Our guide to pages your chatbot can answer is a good handout for clients.

The chat badge is off by default on every plan. On the Agency plan the WordPress admin also shows your logo and menu name.

The Agency plan covers unlimited production sites. Staging and local sites never count.

Each site uses the AI key you add. Many agencies let clients add their own key, often within a free tier.

Yes. On the Agency plan you can export settings and custom answers as a file and import them on another site. API keys are included only if you tick that option.
